dedupe_keys.name: impacts of four london tube strikes on bikeshare use and cycling behaviour

description: This study by Yuanxuan Yang, Roger Beecham, Alison Heppenstall, Andy Turner and Alexis Comber (Journal of Transport Geography, 2021) examines how four London Underground (Tube) strikes changed the use of the London Cycle Hire scheme. Coverage: origin-destination trip data from the scheme and time series of bike availability at docking stations around each strike, analysed with spatiotemporal and graph-based methods. Bikeshare use generally rises during Tube disruptions, but the extent and nature of the rise depend on the type of disruption; a new measure of station pressure shows the scheme quickly reaching saturated capacity and becoming unusable in parts of London. Weekday strikes bring new behaviours and new origin-destination pairs, while weekend strikes consolidate existing patterns, and cyclists are pushed to second or third choice docking stations. Format and access: an open access journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the analysis covers one bikeshare scheme and four events; causes of each change are inferred from patterns. The findings can be used to model mode substitution and dock capacity limits when simulating transit disruptions and the resilience of multimodal urban networks. It relates to the Philadelphia strike study, the TfL Unified API and the TfL cycling infrastructure database in the catalogue.
